reason: The cited evidence (E2) supports that partial recrystallization creates heterogeneous grain structures and improves mechanical properties in a related alloy, but neither E1 nor E2 addresses the target (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy or the critical premise that the caloric order–disorder transition is preserved under such annealing. The caloric preservation premise is entirely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Partial recrystallization annealing can create a heterogeneous grain structure in the target alloy.
A heterogeneous grain structure improves mechanical integrity via load partitioning and back-stress hardening.
The caloric response is driven by an order–disorder transition that is insensitive to grain structure changes.
The proposed annealing will not alter the order–disorder transition or degrade caloric performance.
